events.title: Napoleon Seizes Power in France
events.description: On 18 Brumaire in the French Republican calendar, Napoleon Bonaparte and his allies overthrew the Directory. The coup took place on November 9, 1799. It installed a three-man Consulate with Napoleon as its dominant figure.
events.significance: The coup ended the French Revolution's republican government and started Napoleon's rise. He became emperor within five years, and his rule reshaped Europe.

events.title: Kristallnacht Pogroms Begin
events.description: On the night of November 9, 1938, Nazi authorities and their supporters attacked Jewish communities across Germany and Austria. They smashed shop windows, burned synagogues and killed Jewish people. Tens of thousands of Jewish men were then sent to concentration camps.
events.significance: The night marked a sharp escalation in the Nazi persecution of Jews. It is now remembered as a turning point on the road to the Holocaust.

events.title: Cambodia Gains Independence from France
events.description: On November 9, 1953, Cambodia became fully independent after nearly ninety years as a French protectorate. King Norodom Sihanouk had campaigned for the handover, which came with the transfer of remaining French authority.
events.significance: The date is still celebrated as Cambodia's Independence Day. It was a key step in the end of French colonial rule in Southeast Asia.

events.title: Carl Sagan Is Born
events.description: The astronomer and author Carl Sagan was born in Brooklyn, New York, on November 9, 1934. He became one of the best-known science communicators of the twentieth century. His work included the television series Cosmos.
events.significance: Sagan brought astronomy and planetary science to a mass audience. He also helped inspire the search for life beyond Earth.

events.title: The Berlin Wall Opens
events.description: On the evening of November 9, 1989, East Germany announced that its citizens could cross the border to the West. Crowds gathered at checkpoints, and guards opened the gates. People celebrated on top of the Wall.
events.significance: The opening of the Wall became the defining image of the end of the Cold War. Germany reunified less than a year later.
